title: Duel Decks: Elves vs. Goblins: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "No matter how adept our artistic skill, our effigies can never hope to capture the vibrant beauty of a living elf. Perhaps that is truly why we mourn."
"My tales of war are the stories most asked for around the fires at night, but they're the ones I care least to tell."
"Channel your vitality through me."
In a culture of beauty, the most beautiful are worshipped as gods.
One bone broken for every twig snapped underfoot. —Llanowar penalty for trespassing
From the highest tiers of Dawn's Light Palace to the deepest shade of Wren's Run, the silver notes of the horn shimmer through the air, and all who hear it feel its pull.
The Mirari pulses in his veins.
Even through the Mirari's voice, the elves still hear the call of their kinship.
The ritual of making draws upon the elves' memories and pasts. And elves have long memories and ancient pasts.
"Close your ears to the voice of greed, and you can turn a gift for one into a gift for many."
The goblins laughed as the elf ran away, until more came back.
It drinks fatigue.
Every branch a crossroads, every vine a swift steed.
The faultless and immaculate castes form the lower tiers of elvish society, with the exquisite caste above them. At the pinnacle is the perfect, a consummate blend of aristocrat and predator.
"Life's greatest lessons don't come from focus or concentration. They come from breathing and simply noticing." —Seton, centaur druid
Two times the size, four times the smell.
Diluted, moonglove can etch living tissue. Concentrated, a drop will kill a giant.
The pattern of life can be studied like a book, if you know how to read it.
No matter where you find them, goblins love rocks.
The least popular goblins get the outer caves.
Legends say a djinn gave the goblins a gift they could never hope to master.
Inside even the humblest goblin lurks the potential for far greater things—and far worse.
Akki shells provided good protection when downhill charging became headlong tumbling.
There's always room for one more.
"Let's play 'sled.' Here's how it works: you're the sled."
They poured from the Skirk Ridge like lava, burning and devouring everything in their path.
"Everybody but me—CHARGE!"
"I got it! I got it! I—"
The oil sloshes against his skull as he nears his destination: the Frogtosser Games and the lighting of the Flaming Boggart.
He raged at the world, at his family, at his life. But mostly he just raged.
"Release chaos with me!"
"I order you to volunteer."
He's boss because he's smart enough to get out of the way.
"I like goblins. They make funny little popping sounds when they die." —Braids, dementia summoner
In a shaman's grimy hands, a concoction of dried Skirk Ridge herbs can become the face of panic.
"Auntie Grub had caught a goat, a bleating doe that still squirmed in her arms. At the same time, her warren decided to share with her a sensory greeting of hot tar . . . ." —A tale of Auntie Grub
Boggarts revel in discovering new sensations, from the texture of an otter pellet to the squeak of a dying warren mate.
"Within each of you is the strength of a landslide." —Kumano, to his pupils
"After Auntie brushed the soot from her eyes, she discovered something wonderful: the fire had turned the goat into something that smelled delicious." —A tale of Auntie Grub
